author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Plutarch, Life of Brutus (Plut. Brut.), c. 100-110 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Primary narrative source for Brutus's life. Written ~150 years after his death. Plutarch draws on earlier sources including Brutus's own letters and possibly lost biographies. Some passages are shaped by Plutarch's moralizing interest in Brutus as a virtuous character.

author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
title_en: Letters to Brutus and other correspondence
title_orig: Epistulae ad Brutum, ad Atticum, ad Familiares
citation_detail: Cicero, Letters to Brutus (Epistulae ad Brutum) and other correspondence (ad Atticum, ad Familiares), 44-43 BCE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Contemporary letters between Cicero and Brutus in the months after Caesar's assassination. Essential for understanding Brutus's political thinking and relationship with Cicero. Authenticity of some letters in the ad Brutum collection is disputed. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5: specific letter authenticity needs verification.

author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
citation_detail: Cicero, Brutus (De Claris Oratoribus), 46 BCE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Cicero's dialogue on the history of Roman oratory, dedicated to and featuring Brutus as an interlocutor. Establishes Brutus's intellectual reputation before the assassination. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5: self-serving literary representation by Cicero.

author: Appian of Alexandria
citation_detail: Appian, Civil Wars (Bella Civilia) Books 2-4, c. 150-160 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Detailed narrative of Caesar's assassination and the Liberators' war. Books 2-4 cover 44-42 BCE. Draws on lost sources including Asinius Pollio and Livy.

author: Cassius Dio
citation_detail: Cassius Dio, Roman History Books 44-48, c. 210-230 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Continuous narrative from Caesar's assassination through Philippi. Written ~250 years after events. Draws on Augustan-era and later traditions.

author: Suetonius
citation_detail: Suetonius, Divus Julius (Life of Caesar), c. 119-121 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Suetonius covers Caesar's assassination and notes Brutus's role. The famous 'Et tu, Brute?' (Suet. Jul. 82.2) is recorded as 'καὶ σύ, τέκνον;' in Greek and likely represents later dramatic tradition.

author: Nicolaus of Damascus
citation_detail: Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Augustus (Bios Kaisaros), c. 20 BCE. Fragments in FGrH 90.
notes: Near-contemporary source written under Augustus's patronage. Covers Caesar's assassination in detail. Reflects Augustan perspective. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5: fragmentary preservation, pro-Augustan bias.

author: Ronald Syme
citation_detail: Syme, Ronald (1939). The Roman Revolution. Oxford University Press.
notes: Foundational modern study. Analyzes Brutus's political position and the Liberators' failure as part of the transition from Republic to Principate.

author: Kathryn Tempest
citation_detail: Tempest, Kathryn (2017). Brutus: The Noble Conspirator. Yale University Press.
notes: Recent scholarly biography of Brutus. Analyzes his intellectual development, political career, and the assassination within the context of late Republican political culture.

author: Elizabeth Rawson
title_en: Cassius and Brutus: The Memory of the Liberators
citation_detail: Rawson, Elizabeth (1986). Cassius and Brutus: The Memory of the Liberators. In: Moxon, Smart, and Woodman (eds.), Past Perspectives. Cambridge University Press.
notes: Analyzes how the memory of Brutus and Cassius was constructed, contested, and transmitted in Roman culture.
